title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). G is a stable 'modular graph', the dual graph of a stable marked curve X, and M_G is the corresponding stratum (a multiplicity, i.e. an orbifold or stack) of the Deligne-Mumford compactification. G' is a 'generalization' of G: the graph obtained by smoothing a set C of double points (edges), so that M_G lies in the boundary of the closure of M_{G'}. The tilde/superscript-C objects M^C_G and \widetilde M^C_G are torsors over M_G built from the smoothing parameters at the nodes in C, i.e. the (C^*)^C-frame bundle of the normal bundle ⊕_{c∈C} T_c'⊗T_c'' to the stratum. 𝓜_C is a product of punctured discs or circles.

The previous page built a topos morphism 𝓜_C × \widetilde M^C_G → M_{G'}. It plays the role of the inclusion of the deleted tubular neighbourhood V*_{G,G'} of M_G in M_{G'}, and fits in a cartesian square over SP_{G'}, a torsor or universal-cover-like object. That page then supposes a section of M^C_G → M_G exists ('y en a-t-il toujours ??', added 'je pense que oui'). Under that assumption the deleted neighbourhood becomes a product, giving the cartesian square SP_G × 𝓜_C → SP_{G'} over P_C × 𝓜_C → M_{G'}.

This page continues: then, 'in a very strong sense (worth making explicit)', P_C × 𝓜_C is identified with a slice of a tubular neighbourhood. A crossed-out clause had P_C as its boundary. This is the topological model needed to define the Teichmüller groupoid: base points 'at infinity' near the boundary strata, and the paths joining a stratum to a less degenerate one.

Programme. The most motivating cases are:
- G' = G^♮, the extreme generalization, i.e. the open stratum M_{g,ν}.
- G of modular dimension 0 or 1 and G' of modular dimension ≤ 2.
- In particular 'immediate generalizations', where C is a single node.
This is exactly the 'two-level' principle of the Esquisse: the Teichmüller tower is generated in modular dimension ≤1, with relations in dimension ≤2.

The page then treats modular dimension 0. Here Σ_v (3g_v − 3 + n_v) = 0, so every component of X is a P^1 with 3 special points (margin: genus 0, 'order' 3): a maximally degenerate curve, i.e. a pants decomposition. Since a P^1 with an I-marking, card I = 3, is rigid (unique up to unique isomorphism), X is determined up to unique isomorphism by G. M_G is a point multiplicity, essentially BAut(G).

To build explicit topological models, he takes the complex projective line with 0, 1, ∞ and its automorphism group S_3 (called G_3). The next page puts on it the unique S_3-invariant round metric: the three points form an equilateral triangle on a great circle. He then chooses S_3-stable systems of disjoint metric discs around the three points, depending on a radius parameter 0<ρ≤1. This yields a canonical, S_3-symmetric 'standard pair of pants' with marked boundary points, from which nearby smooth curves can be glued (plumbing). It is a rigid, symmetric model for the Lego pieces of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The hope on the previous page that a section of M^C_G over M_G always exists ('je pense que oui') is doubtful at the level of multiplicities/orbifolds. The normal bundle of a boundary stratum is a tensor product of tangent lines (ψ-type classes), which need not be trivial. Example: a vertex of type (1,1) gives ψ = λ on M_{1,1}, of order 12 in Pic. So an orbifold section of the associated C^*-torsor fails in general. A section exists on suitable covers, e.g. Teichmüller space, which is presumably what is actually used.
'M_G est la multiplicité ponctuelle' is correct only as a stack with residual automorphism group Aut(X) = Aut(G) (as a marked graph). Not an error, but the gerbe structure matters for the groupoid.

'Métrique ... unique invariante par G_3' (next page) holds only within round (constant curvature) conformal metrics up to scale. Arbitrary S_3-invariant metrics are not unique. The context makes the intended meaning clear.

ideas.what: Deleted tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum M_G in M_{G'} modelled as (torsor of smoothing parameters) × (punctured polydisc), with a product decomposition when a section exists
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing / normal-crossings neighbourhood of boundary strata of Deligne-Mumford compactification; tangential base points at boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara-Nakamura (maximal degeneration, Schottky-Mumford curves, 1997); standard plumbing coordinates (Wolpert, Bers, Fay)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions base points at infinity / tangential base points for the Teichmüller tower, without this formalism

ideas.what: Restricting attention to strata of modular dimension ≤1 and generalizations of modular dimension ≤2 (immediate generalizations: smoothing one node)
ideas.modern_name: Two-level principle for the Teichmüller tower (generators in dim ≤1, relations in dim ≤2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme); proved/formalized by Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Bakalov-Kirillov, Moore-Seiberg

ideas.what: Modular dimension 0 strata = curves all of whose components are 3-pointed P^1; rigid, determined by the graph
ideas.modern_name: Maximally degenerate stable curves / pants decompositions as 0-cells (vertices) of the Teichmüller groupoid

ideas.what: Canonical S_3-symmetric round model of P^1 − {0,1,∞} with symmetric disc systems (radius parameter ρ) as a standard pair of pants
ideas.modern_name: Standard/symmetric pair of pants used in Lego-Teichmüller constructions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various; Bakalov-Kirillov use standard spheres with holes; hyperbolic Fenchel-Nielsen pants more common

missed.claim: Grothendieck wants a 'very strong' identification of P_C × 𝓜_C with a slice of a tubular neighbourhood of M_G in M_{G'}, as a topos-level model of the deleted neighbourhood. He leaves it to be 'made explicit', and the existence of the required global section is left as an open question. The modern equivalent (plumbing coordinates, Ihara-Nakamura tangential base points) exists, but not in this topos-theoretic form.
missed.quote: dans un sens très fort (qu'il vaudrait la peine peut-être d'expliciter) P_C × 𝓜_C s'identifie à une [tranche] de voisinage tubulaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is a precursor of the now-standard boundary/tangential base point machinery for the Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower. It contains no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a consistent working-out of the Esquisse programme: tubular neighbourhoods of boundary strata, the two-level principle, maximally degenerate curves as rigid base points, and a symmetric pants model. Later literature (Ihara-Nakamura, Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Bakalov-Kirillov) covers all of this. Nothing here seems both finished and absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: Line 1-2: 'qu'il vaudrait la peine peut-être d'expliciter', not 'qu'il conviendrait la peine'.
'une trace de voisinage tubulaire' is more plausibly 'une tranche de voisinage tubulaire' (reading uncertain).
'G' = G^♮ (généralisation ... de G)': the adjective is unclear; 'maximale' fits both the handwriting and the sense (open stratum) better than 'minimale'.
'correspondant au cas où C est réduit à un ... élément' (a single node) rather than 'point double ... clivement'.
Margin: likely 'ie les composantes de X sont de genre 0, d'ordre 3' (X, not C).

'grâce au fait qu'une droite projective munie d'un I-marquage, où card I = 3, est définie à isom. unique près. Donc la multiplicité M_G est la multiplicité ponctuelle'; the duplicated garbled lines in the machine transcription should be merged.
'la droite projective ℙ_ℂ avec les trois pts marqués' (complex projective line), not 'ℙ_C' indexed by the node set C.
